title: Using a Salary Inclusive of Super Calculator to Convert Hourly Rates to Annual Pay
description: Convert your hourly rate to annual salary including super with our salary inclusive of super calculator. Understand 38-hour weeks, casual loading, and tax estimates for 2026–27.
salarySummary: For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, annual gross pay is the hourly rate multiplied by 38 then by 52, with super paid on top.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect my annual pay estimate?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% on top of the base hourly rate, as set by the Fair Work Commission. When you use a salary inclusive of super calculator, you should enter your base rate (not including loading) and then select the casual loading option. The calculator will add 25% to the hourly rate before multiplying by hours and weeks. For example, the national minimum wage of $26.44 per hour becomes $33.05 per hour with casual loading. This higher rate is then used to estimate annual gross pay, and super is calculated on that loaded amount.

faqs.q: Is super included in the annual gross figure or paid on top?
faqs.a: Super is paid on top of your cash salary. The super guarantee rate is 12% of ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. In a salary inclusive of super calculator, the annual gross figure shown is your cash salary before tax. Super is estimated separately and added to show total employment cost. If an offer says 'package includes super', the advertised figure already contains the super component, so your cash salary is lower. Always check whether the rate you enter is base salary or total package.

faqs.q: What tax and Medicare are deducted from my estimated take-home pay?
faqs.a: For 2026–27, the resident tax rates are: nil on the first $18,200, 15% from $18,201 to $45,000, 30% from $45,001 to $135,000, 37% from $135,001 to $190,000, and 45% above $190,000. The Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income, with reduced rates for low-income earners. The salary inclusive of super calculator applies these rates to your estimated annual gross pay, but it does not deduct HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary sacrifice amounts. The result is a budgeting estimate, not a precise payslip.

bodyMarkdown:
## How a Salary Inclusive of Super Calculator Works

When you have an hourly rate or a salary offer, the quickest way to see the annual picture is to multiply your hourly rate by the hours you work each week and then by the number of paid weeks in a year. For a full-time employee, the standard assumption is 38 ordinary hours per week and 52 paid weeks. That gives you the annual gross cash salary. From there, a **salary inclusive of super calculator** adds the employer super contribution on top and estimates the tax and Medicare that will be withheld.

### The Basic Formula

Annual gross cash salary = hourly rate × hours per week × 52.

If you work 38 hours per week at $45.00 per hour, the calculation is:

$45.00 × 38 × 52 = $88,920 per year before tax.

This figure does not include super. The super guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid by the employer on top of your cash salary. For the same $88,920, the super contribution would be $10,670 (12% of $88,920), making the total employment cost $99,590.

### Fortnightly and Weekly Figures

To see your pay over a shorter period, divide the annual figure by 26 for a fortnight or by 52 for a week. Using the example above:

- Weekly: $88,920 ÷ 52 = $1,710.00
- Fortnightly: $88,920 ÷ 26 = $3,420.00

These are gross amounts before tax. The calculator also shows estimated take-home pay after applying the 2026–27 tax rates and the Medicare levy.

## National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The Fair Work Commission sets the national minimum wage each year. From 1 July 2026, the rate is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. This is the minimum for adult employees not covered by an award or agreement. Most employees, however, are covered by an award that sets higher minimum rates for their industry and role. The [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page on this site lists the current rates, and the [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman provide detailed tables for each award.

Award rates often include penalty rates for weekends, evenings, or overtime. The simple hourly-to-annual formula does not account for those extras. It assumes the same rate every hour, every week. If your role regularly attracts penalty rates, your actual annual earnings will be higher than the estimate.

## Casual Loading

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. When you use the [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) option on this site, the calculator adds 25% to the rate you enter. For example, if the base rate is $26.44, the casual rate becomes $33.05 per hour. The annual estimate then uses the loaded rate.

**Important:** Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading. The calculator applies the loading automatically when you check the box. Enter the base rate as stated in your award or agreement.

## Super Paid on Top

Super is a separate payment from your cash salary. The super guarantee requires employers to pay 12% of your ordinary earnings into a super fund, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. In the [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) section, you can see how super affects total remuneration. If an employer offers a salary package 'including super', the advertised figure already contains the super component. For example, a $100,000 package including super means your cash salary is about $89,286 and the super is $10,714. A salary inclusive of super calculator lets you switch between 'plus super' and 'including super' to compare offers accurately.

## Average Weekly Earnings Context

The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports average weekly earnings for full-time adults at $2,083.70 per week (May 2026). That equates to an annual cash salary of about $108,352. When all employees (including part-time) are counted, the average is $1,579.20 per week, or $82,118 annually. These figures help you benchmark your rate against the broader market. See the [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page for more detail.

## Tax Estimates

The calculator applies the 2026–27 resident tax scale:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15%
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30%
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37%
- $190,001 and above: 45%

Medicare levy is 2% of taxable income, with reduced rates for low-income earners. The calculator uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of this reference. The estimate does not include HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary sacrifice. For a more detailed breakdown, visit the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page.

## Limitations of the Calculator

This tool provides an estimate based on consistent weekly hours and a single hourly rate. It does not model unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary packaging. The annual figure is a guide for budgeting and comparing job offers, not a determination of your actual pay or tax liability. Always consult your award, enterprise agreement, or a qualified adviser for precise figures.

By entering your base hourly rate and selecting the casual loading option if applicable, you can quickly see your estimated annual cash salary, super contribution, and approximate take-home pay. The salary inclusive of super calculator is designed to give you a clear picture of what your hourly rate means over a full year.
